headline: GOLIATH GOT.V GOLDEN TRIANGLE: GOLDEN GATE ZONE EXPANDS 320m NORTHEAST — 9.87 g/t Au OVER 5m PROVES SUREBET OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Goliath Resources (TSXV: GOT; OTCQX: GOTRF)
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSXV: GOT) released a second batch of assay results on August 10, 2026 from its 50,000-metre program at the Golddigger Property in BC's Golden Triangle, confirming that the Golden Gate Zone has now expanded 320 metres to the northeast of previously known boundaries, with the zone remaining open in every direction. The headline intercept returned 9.87 g/t gold over 5.00 metres. This is separate from the earlier August 6 batch that expanded the Bonanza Zone; today's data specifically confirms the Golden Gate Zone's northeast extension, growing the total discovery footprint. Of 35 holes drilled in the 2026 program so far, 20 have intersected visible gold — with 15 still pending assay, meaning further expansion results are on the way.

headline: MALAYSIA WEIGHS CONDITIONAL EASING OF 2024 RAW RARE EARTH EXPORT BAN — US, AUSTRALIA, FRANCE, INDIA PRESS FOR ACCESS
snippet: Malaysia is assessing whether to allow some exports of unprocessed rare earths after banning raw rare earth exports in 2024 to incentivize domestic processing investment. Deputy Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh cited mounting pressure from Malaysian states and foreign investors — specifically the US, Australia, France, and India — as Western governments intensify efforts to diversify critical mineral supply chains following China's 2025 heavy rare earth export restrictions. Any easing would likely be small, tied to research and development uses abroad, and conditional on investment-in-Malaysia and technology-transfer requirements. For junior rare earth developers in allied nations — notably Canada, Australia, and the US — the shift confirms the post-China-export-controls scramble: Western nations are now approaching Malaysia, which hosts the Lynas Rare Earths processing complex and sits atop significant rare earth resources, as a swing supply source for heavy rare earths not available from within their own borders.

headline: NEVADA TUNGSTEN JACKPOT: 1.78M TONNES IS 5X LARGEST KNOWN US DEPOSIT — BUT NASA LAND WITHDRAWAL BLOCKS KEY ZONE
source_name: IndexBox / 3 Proton Lithium (Railroad Valley Minerals Project)
snippet: 3 Proton Lithium confirmed August 7, 2026 an inferred resource of 1.78 million tonnes of tungsten at its Railroad Valley Minerals Project in Nye County, Nevada — more than five times the second-largest known US tungsten deposit — alongside 31 million tonnes of measured lithium carbonate equivalent, 533 million tonnes of potash, and 87 million tonnes of borates in the same salt complex. The combined resource is estimated at approximately USD 3.5 trillion. The critical obstacle: a 17-square-mile section covering what may be the highest-grade tungsten zone sits beneath a 20-year mining withdrawal NASA imposed in 2023 to protect a flat lakebed it uses to calibrate Earth-observing satellites. Tungsten prices have surged approximately 600% since February 2025 on Chinese export restrictions — tungsten is essential for cutting tools, armor-piercing ammunition, and aerospace components, and the US stopped domestic tungsten mining a decade ago. The discovery puts the US at a decision point: satellite calibration infrastructure versus strategic mineral self-sufficiency, with the Trump administration reported to be prioritising the project but production still at least five years away.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLD & SILVER SURGE PAVES THE WAY — IS PLATINUM THE NEXT METAL TO EXPLODE HIGHER?
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published analysis on August 8, 2026 examining platinum's structural investment case in the context of the prior week's explosive gold and silver rally. The analysis highlights that platinum — which doubled gold's performance in 2025 after years of underperformance — enters August 2026 with a fundamentally distinct supply-demand profile from gold and silver: a structural supply deficit driven by South African production constraints, Russian export uncertainty, and surging demand from hydrogen fuel cell and industrial catalyst applications. With gold near $4,340 and silver above $64, platinum's relative cheapness — historically a proxy for whether industrial demand is outpacing monetary demand — creates a convergence trade for investors who missed the first leg of the precious metals bull cycle. The platinum group metals (PGMs) have historically lagged gold by 3–6 months at bull market inflection points before catching up sharply.

headline: ABEN GOLD ABM.V YUKON: FIRST DRILL TURNS AT JUSTIN GOLD-TUNGSTEN — POW ZONE TARGETED 25km FROM HISTORIC CANTUNG MINE
source_name: Investing News Network / Aben Gold Corp (TSXV: ABM)
snippet: Aben Gold Corp. (TSXV: ABM) announced August 10, 2026 that the first drill pad at the POW Zone of its Justin Gold-Tungsten Project in southeastern Yukon Territory has been completed and diamond drilling has commenced. The 1,300-metre 2026 program targets two high-priority areas — the POW Zone and the Lost Ace Zone, 2 kilometres to the northwest — identified through historical drilling reinterpretation and reassessment of historical tungsten assays previously overlooked during lower-tungsten-price environments. Justin is located 25km from the Cantung Mine, historically one of Canada's most significant tungsten operations. The timing is notable: tungsten has surged approximately 600% since February 2025 on Chinese export controls, making historical tungsten-bearing gold systems like Justin economically material at grades that were previously considered sub-economic by-product concentrations.

headline: SILVER $64+ MONDAY AFTER PAYROLLS SURGE: FED RATE CUT BET ACCELERATES — SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE WEEK ABOVE $60
snippet: Silver extended its payrolls-driven advance on Monday August 10, rising to $64.24 per ounce — the highest level since late January 2026's all-time high complex — as September futures opened at $63.80 (+0.5% from Friday's close). The driver is the same as last week's $300 gold surge: July nonfarm payrolls came in at -23,000 versus a +180,000 consensus, pulling forward Fed rate-cut expectations and weakening the dollar. Silver has now held above $60 for seven consecutive weeks, a technical durability indicator that bulls cite as evidence this is a structural advance rather than a payrolls-spike. The gold-silver ratio, which compressed from 70x toward 66x last week, is the central metric to watch this week: if silver outperforms further (ratio falling toward 60x), historical precedent from 2010–2011 and 2020 suggests the retail silver buying cycle — which has historically driven the final 40–60% of silver's bull market move — is beginning.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT REPORT AUG 7: GOLD MANAGED MONEY REBUILDS TO 130K CONTRACTS — DOLLAR INDEX VULNERABLE AT 200-DAY MA
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitments of Traders report for the week ending August 4, 2026 (published August 7) shows gold managed money net long positioning rebuilding to approximately 130,766 contracts — up from the 90,000-range lows of the July correction but still significantly below the 200,000+ contracts seen at January 2026's all-time high, confirming substantial speculative buying capacity remains. The US Dollar Index (DXY) is flagged as a key technical vulnerability: with DXY testing its 200-day moving average from above following the payrolls miss, a decisive break lower would remove the dollar headwind that capped gold through the June–July correction and could accelerate the current rally. The COT analysis — combining gold positioning runway, silver's near-record-low managed money positioning relative to price, and dollar index technical breakdown risk — presents a three-factor bullish setup that the author argues makes the current week's CPI and PPI prints the pivotal near-term catalysts for the next directional move in the sector.

headline: CHARTS OF THE WEEK 8/9/2026: GOLD +$250 IN FIVE SESSIONS, MINERS SOAR, SECOND US PORPHYRY COPPER DISCOVERY IN A MONTH
source_name: Robert Sinn / The Week in Charts (Substack)
snippet: Market analyst Robert Sinn published his weekly charts review on August 9, 2026 documenting what he calls a watershed week for gold and mining stocks: gold's $250+ advance in five sessions following the July payrolls miss, accompanied by GDX surging over 14% and GDXJ outperforming on junior leverage. The piece also highlights what Sinn describes as 'another porphyry copper discovery in the USA' — the second significant US porphyry copper announcement in a single month, following BCM Resources' Thompson Knolls Utah result (already covered). The confluence of a gold breakout driving junior equity re-rating alongside simultaneous major copper porphyry discoveries in the US Southwest is, in Sinn's framing, the structural setup that characterized the most productive periods of the 2003–2008 resource bull: gold leading, juniors following, and copper discovery catalysts pulling generalist capital into the sector.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICE $94/LB LEADS SPOT AT $86.50 — UTILITIES AND AI DATA CENTRES COMPETE FOR LONG-TERM SUPPLY CONTRACTS
snippet: Long-term uranium contract prices have diverged significantly from spot prices in August 2026, with term contracts being signed at $94 per pound of U3O8 while spot trades near $86.50/lb — a $7.50/lb premium that reflects utilities' urgent desire to lock in supply years ahead and their acceptance of above-spot pricing to do so. The term-price premium is being amplified by a new class of buyers: AI-driven data centre operators including Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon are competing with traditional nuclear utilities for long-term power purchase agreements tied to nuclear reactors, creating incremental uranium demand that utilities had not factored into their fuel procurement schedules. For retail investors tracking the uranium sector, the term-spot spread is one of the most reliable indicators of structural market tightness: when utilities and corporates are willing to pay materially more for future delivery than for immediate delivery, it signals a market that prices in supply risk over the next 5–10 years — the window within which no significant new uranium mines can be brought to production from greenfield status.
